messages.subject: Re: Using data.table with renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,
There's been quite a bit of work done around Renjin and databases over the last year, but I don't think anyone's looked at the sqldf package in particular.

It looks like it is now failing because it attempts to load a (native) Sqlite extension DLL, which is either already incorporated into the build of sqlite we're using from xerial or may not be available:
https://bitbucket.org/xerial/sqlite-jdbc

You can try stubbing out this initExtension() method in https://github.com/bedatadriven/RSQLIte and see if the rest of the package's functionality works.

Pull requests welcome on both projects!

Alex

Hi Ravi,
It looks like the dummies() function was passing the argument contrasts.arg = FALSE instead of contrasts.arg = NULL to the model.matrix function, which Renjin's implementation couldn't handle. I've added a check for this as it looks like contrasts.arg = FALSE became legal around R 2.15. Your example above now runs under Renjin 0.8.2326.

I took a look at some of the other examples from the dummy package that are failing under Renjin. In the remaining cases, however, it looks like since the package was first released in 2012, the dummy.data.frame no longer works in GNU R 3.3. We strive to stay compatible with the latest version of GNU R, so I would not expect this function to work under Renjin either. If you need this function, you can consider submitting a patch to the package's author.

Best,
Alex

Thanks Parham,

that solved my issue.
I was missing the fact that I need to set the "class".

After that, I discovered (it is not covered by the example) that the attribute "row.names" is also supposed to be set.

I think a good solution is something like:

 dataFrame.setAttribute(Symbols.ROW_NAMES, new IntSequence(1, 1, length))

Maybe it would be a good idea to give prominence to these facts in the interoperability documentation.

thanks,
Francesco
